solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Ardent, he may be following a cause

definitions.note: used adjectivally: sticking to and supporting a cause

indicators.note: the letters of the two words may be rearranged into something else, so they are mixed up

explanation.surface: A passionate man might well be a supporter of some campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals the rearrangement of ARDENT and HE.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a supporter or follower of a party, cause or creed, and as an adjective means sticking to one.

clue.text: Deny a key's been stupidly mislaid outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the key letter, enclosing it
done stupidly, the letters of the word are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone denies having foolishly lost a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' turns MISLAID into DISLAIM, and 'outside' wraps that round C.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclaim something is to renounce or refuse to acknowledge it, a synonym of deny.

clue.text: Returns from work

parts.note: reads like someone coming home from the office, but returns here means money gained through a job, as in tax terms

explanation.definitionFit: Earned income is the tax term for money received from employment, the returns of one's labour.

clue.text: Number of the French in uniform

indicators.note: the French article is placed inside the word for uniform

parts.note: even means uniform, regular
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Asks how many French people are wearing uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a number, the one after ten.

clue.text: Drop in rent

definitions.meaning: a drop of water from the eye

explanation.surface: A fall in the rent someone pays.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear is both a drop from the eye and a rip in fabric, which is what a rent is.

clue.text: Where barristers practise drinking?

definitions.meaning: lawyers are called to and practise ... of the court
someone drinking in a pub is standing at the counter

explanation.surface: Asks where lawyers work: in the pub, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both practising as a barrister and being at a pub counter, as drinkers are.

clue.text: Small number turned up at church in the past

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: no. is the short form of number
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A handful of worshippers appeared at the service long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some time in the past.

clue.text: A child among children, though mature

indicators.note: the pieces are placed among, so inside, the word for children

parts.note: seed means offspring, descendants, in the biblical sense
a son is a child

explanation.surface: One youngster among several, yet grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: SEED for children is the old biblical sense of offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned means experienced or matured, like wood left to age.

clue.text: Indoor transport

definitions.meaning: a way in, the door into a place
to delight or enrapture, as a verb

explanation.surface: Inside transport, such as a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance is a doorway in; to entrance is to enrapture, which is what transport means as a verb.

clue.text: In retreat a holy man leads king and emperor

indicators.note: leading means coming in front of the next piece
retreating means going backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ST is short for saint
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A holy man on retreat guides a king and an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retreat' reverses A ST to give TSA, which 'leads' R.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia.

clue.text: Yet three sevens turn out to be around fifty

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the Roman fifty
the letters turn out to make something different, so they are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Arithmetic nonsense: three sevens come to roughly fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's sum is nonsense: 'Yet' at the front is the definition, used as an adverb meaning however, and 'to be' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevertheless and yet both mean in spite of that, however.

clue.text: Yet this could be just one word — life

definitions.text: Yet this could be just one word — life

parts.words: Yet this could be just one word — life
parts.note: a grammatical paradox about a sentence of one word, resolved by the prison sense: a judge saying 'life' passes a lengthy term

explanation.definitionFit: A life term in prison is a lengthy judicial sentence, though the judge may pronounce it in a single word.

clue.text: Enthusiast on trip to see erotic performance

indicators.note: in an across entry, on means set before the next piece

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
to trip is to dance, as in trip the light fantastic

explanation.surface: A fan goes on a journey to watch a risqué show.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan dance is a burlesque routine where the performer is concealed by large fans, an erotic act.

clue.text: Hail enters two points in part of roof

indicators.note: the greeting goes inside the pair of compass letters

parts.note: E and S, east and south, are compass points
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting

explanation.surface: Hailstones get into a couple of spots in the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The eaves are the overhanging lower edge of a roof.

clue.text: Speak at tedious length? Exactly

definitions.meaning: to talk on and on boringly

explanation.surface: A complaint about someone droning on, answered with agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang on is informal for droning on, and also British slang for exactly right.

clue.text: The last word in steam engines

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the two words

explanation.surface: Claims steam locomotives are the finest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last word in' looks like praise; 'in' is the signal and the definition is 'The last word'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the end of a prayer, so it is the closing word.

clue.text: Union gets everybody a nice settlement

parts.note: all means everybody

indicators.note: the letters settle into a new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trade union wins a good deal for all its members.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or association formed for mutual benefit.

clue.text: Sweetheart long gone

parts.note: over means finished, gone

explanation.surface: A former partner, long gone from someone's life.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover is a sweetheart, someone loved romantically.

clue.text: Pushed the boat out in Paris?

definitions.text: Pushed the boat out in Paris?

parts.words: Pushed the boat out in Paris?
parts.note: pushing a boat out means leaving the riverside; in Paris the south side of the Seine has a famous name for that bank

explanation.definitionFit: The Left Bank is the south bank of the Seine in Paris, and a boat pushed off has left the bank.

clue.text: Small child to go out of control

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A toddler running wild.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that skids slides out of control.

clue.text: New form of travel in space

indicators.note: a new form of the letters is made, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A novel way of journeying through outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a space or gap between two things or times.

clue.text: Allow to escape the cross-Channel swell

parts.note: le is the French for the, from across the English Channel
a swell or toff is an upper-class, smartly dressed person

explanation.surface: A sea swell in the Channel lets a boat get away.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF and swell are British slang for a posh, fashionable person; 'swell' looks like a wave.
explanation.definitionFit: To let off is to release or excuse someone from punishment, allowing escape.

clue.text: Obtaining reason for absence, ticks one off

indicators.note: the letters go off, out of their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher marking a register ticks off a pupil whose excuse has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick note is a doctor's or parent's letter excusing someone's absence through illness.

clue.text: Half turn next to church and the sound of bells

indicators.note: the two pieces sit side by side
turned round, the word is read backwards

parts.note: semi means half, as in semicircle

explanation.surface: Bells ring out beside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimes are the ringing tones made by a set of bells.

clue.text: A staged production

parts.note: sounds like a theatrical show, but means manufacturing done in stages along a moving line

explanation.definitionFit: On an assembly line a product is built in stages, each worker adding a part.

clue.text: Drinks up on board

annotationWithheld.why: Drinks up on board (4): UP inside SS, where 'on board' is both the indicator and the source of SS (steamship), one phrase doing two jobs

clue.text: The key to a US university education?

definitions.text: The key to a US university education?

parts.words: The key to a US university education?
parts.note: a brand of lock and key shares its name with an Ivy League university in Connecticut

explanation.definitionFit: Yale is a well-known make of lock and key, and also an Ivy League university.

clue.text: Fleet vehicle returning at end of day

indicators.note: going back, the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A lorry heading back at close of day.
explanation.definitionFit: A navy is a nation's fleet of warships.

clue.text: Chelsea's opener precedes painful play in important match

indicators.note: comes before, so it goes first in the answer
the opening letter of the word is taken
the letters are allowed to play, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chelsea's first goal comes before a painful showing in the big game.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a London football club; 'play' rearranges PAINFUL into UPFINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cup Final is the deciding match of a knockout football competition such as the FA Cup.

clue.text: Daisy enters city from the West

indicators.note: the flower name is placed inside the city name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A girl called Daisy arrives in a city having come from the West.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy looks like a name. ELY is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Easterly can mean moving towards the east, which is travelling from the west.
